evals.prompt: Yesterday our support agent told a customer they could get a refund under last quarter's policy. The policy changed three weeks ago. Make sure this never happens again.
evals.expected_output: The incident is reconstructed, classified as grounding / parametric-answer or stale-source-served with the reasoning shown, a JSON eval case is written with assertions from the closed set, the case is validated by running scripts/validate-eval.mjs, and the guard is set to run on every change.
assertions: The failure is classified to one primary taxonomy mode with evidence
A complete JSON case file is produced
scripts/validate-eval.mjs is actually run and reported passing
Assertions use only types from the closed set

evals.prompt: Here is our postmortem: the billing agent called the charge API twice for the same invoice because the first call timed out and it retried without checking. Turn this into a regression test.
evals.expected_output: Classified as tool-use / swallowed-error (or duplicate-action if framed as coordination), with a case whose fixture makes the tool fail or time out and whose assertions check the agent surfaces the failure and does not double-charge.
assertions: The classification is in the tool-use or coordination category with the mode named
The case fixture reproduces the timeout or failure condition
An assertion checks the charge is not issued twice or the failure is surfaced
The validator is run on the case

evals.prompt: Our database fell over last night and the whole site was down for two hours. Can you write this up as an eval case?
evals.expected_output: The skill declines or redirects: there is no AI agent in this incident, so generic incident tooling applies, not this skill.
assertions: No agent eval case is fabricated for a pure infrastructure outage
The response points out the skill covers AI agent incidents and suggests the right path
